MS1#0.quote: Located on a 15-km-long horseshoe ridge with the grand Himalayas as a backdrop, Mussoorie spreads across at a height of 2,000 m above sea level.

MS2#0.quote: A Britisher, Captain Frederick Young, accompanied by an official named FJ Shore, had climbed up the hill from the Doon valley in 1827

MS3#0.quote: Many famous personalities have made Mussoorie their home – most notable being authors Ruskin Bond and Bill Aitken.

MS4#0.quote: The best time to visit Mussoorie is during summers, as it offers respite from the scorching summer heat. However, if you are looking for a secluded holiday, come here during winters to witness the snowfall.

MS5#0.quote: This grey and mauve coloured strip appears like a false horizon and is referred to as the ‘winterline.’ Visible from mid-October to mid-January tourists especially flock to the hill station to witness the winterline.

MS6#0.quote: The nearest airport is Jolly Grant at Dehradun (82 km). Taxis are available from the airport.

MS8#0.quote: It is the main shopping area in Mussoorie. Located in the heart of the town, Mall Road connects the two bazaars, Kulri bazaar and Library Chowk.

MS9#0.quote: This is the highest point on the Mall road, you need to take a cable car ride to reach the summit of Gun Hill.

MS9#1.quote: A gun was installed atop this hill by the British in 1865, which used to be fired daily at noon to indicate the time

MS10#0.quote: It is suitable for walking and offers beautiful sunset views of the Himalayas. A superb rock formation, with a life-like resemblance to a sitting camel, can be seen from this spot.

MS11#0.quote: Situated at an altitude of 2,438 m above sea level, Lal Tibba is the highest hill in Mussoorie. The view to the north and the snow-capped peaks is stunning and best at sunrise.

MS12#0.quote: Situated at the east end of town, Landour is a British-era cantonment named after Llanddowror, a remote village in southwest Wales.

MS12#1.quote: The Landour Bazaar is a very popular shopping area.

MS13#0.quote: many houses in Landour are inspired by Scottish author Sir Walter Scott’s novels, with names such as Kenilworth, Ivanhoe, Waverly and Woodstock (now a famous school).

MS14#0.quote: Located about 15 km on the Yamunotri road, Kempty Falls is a popular and picturesque waterfall, located in the beautiful valley surrounded by high mountains.

MS15#0.quote: At Park Estate are the remains of the building and laboratory of Sir George Everest, the Surveyor-General of India from 1830 to 1843.

MS15#1.quote: It is 6 km from Gandhi Chowk and a scenic walk from Library Bazaar, although accessible by road transport to at least Haathi Paon.

MS16#0.quote: The place provides a view of Doon Valley on one side and a panoramic view of the Aglar River valley and the peaks of the Himalayan ranges on the other. The tourism department is developing this house as a museum.

MS17#0.quote: Surkanda Devi Temple can be reached after a 2 km trek from the village Kaddukhal.

MS17#1.quote: The temple is one of the most popular Shakti Peeths of India.

MS18#0.quote: Built in 1836, it is considered to be among the oldest churches in the Himalayan ranges built by Britishers.

MS19#0.quote: Known as Botanical gardens of Mussoorie in pre-Independence era, the Municipal Gardens or the Company Bagh has a variety of beautiful flowers and an amusement park too.

MS20#0.quote: Located about 8 km from Mussoorie on Mussoorie-Dehradun road, it has different ponds for bathing.

MS20#1.quote: Located about 9 km from Mussoorie, you need to cover the last 1.5 km on foot to reach Jharipani Falls.

MS21#0.quote: The artificial lake developed recently about 6 km on the way from Mussoorie, on Dehradun road watch ducks swimming, ride a paddle boat and enjoy amazing views of Doon Valley.

MS22#0.quote: Visit Mussoorie Adventure Park to try hands at some of the best adventures like zip-lining, rock climbing etc.

MS22#1.quote: The Hathipaon trail will take you through the forest as you come across a variety of flora and fauna.

MS23#0.quote: Take prior permission from the forest officials before angling.
